note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Repetition is not accumulating evidence: convergence theory, answer-shift prediction, and empirical validation

nodes.name: Accumulating-evidence intuition
nodes.description: A widely held but unexamined intuition treats repeated contextual assertions as accumulating evidence, so that sufficient repetition of a candidate answer should always alter a model's prediction.

nodes.name: Heterogeneous repetition effects
nodes.description: Under a controlled single-round setting where only repetition varies, LLM predictions behave heterogeneously: some flip immediately, some change only after substantial repetition, some saturate early, and some stay stable under unbounded repetition.

nodes.name: Controlled repetition setup
nodes.description: The analysis uses inputs of the form y||x||...||x||z, with a query prefix y, a loop template x repeated N times, and a suffix z, at a fixed suffix target position, isolating repetition from added evidence or multi-turn interaction.

nodes.name: RoPE logits are bounded
nodes.description: With RoPE, attention logits are finite trigonometric polynomials in relative distance, hence uniformly bounded (Proposition 3.2).

nodes.name: Representations converge as repetition grows
nodes.description: For a decoder-only Transformer under the stated architecture assumptions, the final-layer target representation at every layer converges to a finite limit as N goes to infinity (Theorem 3.6), proved by layerwise induction.

nodes.name: Repetition is not accumulating evidence
nodes.description: Because representations converge to stable query-dependent limits, repeated assertions do not act as accumulating evidence and may fail to alter a prediction even under unbounded repetition, while in other cases a flip is inevitable.

nodes.name: Answer-shift metric and limit estimator
nodes.description: The answer-shift g(ea,eb) projects the final representation onto the answer-embedding difference direction; its infinite-repetition limit is estimated from a single forward pass at large N via Monte Carlo estimates of the loop attention terms.

nodes.name: Layers converge empirically at N=1000
nodes.description: At N=1000 on OpenBookQA, MINTAKA and SimpleQA, a large fraction of layers (typically over 90% at tolerance 0.1) show negligible residual variation in attention and FFN answer-shift contributions across six LLMs.

nodes.name: KL divergence plateaus
nodes.description: KL divergence between next-token distributions at different repetition lengths plateaus as repetition grows, showing answer-level distribution stabilization.

nodes.name: Estimator matches forward shifts
nodes.description: The representation-level estimate of the limiting answer shift closely tracks the forward-computed output answer shift on OpenBookQA at N=1000 across models, with points concentrated on the diagonal.

nodes.name: Predicting answer preference changes
nodes.description: The sign of the estimated shift predicts repetition-induced preference changes across Transfer, Correct and Mislead regimes at N=500/750/1000, with mean accuracy around 80-86% (mean F1 up to about 92% for Transfer).

nodes.name: Consistent with sycophancy benchmarks
nodes.description: The stability measure shows trends broadly consistent with prior evaluations on SYCON, Farm, BeHonest and SycoEval, apart from a few exceptions.

isolated_nodes.name: Robustness depends on query and model
isolated_nodes.description: Susceptibility to input-level manipulation is not uniform but depends systematically on both the query and the model; robustness assessments should distinguish intrinsically stable inputs from vulnerable ones.

isolated_nodes.name: Repetition works only along malleable directions
isolated_nodes.description: Contextual repetition changes predictions only when it aligns with malleable inference directions; otherwise inference converges to a stable regime where more repetition is ineffective.

isolated_nodes.name: Six models across three families
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments cover six LLMs (Falcon3-7B/3B-Base, Mistral-7B-v0.1, Apollo-1-4B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen2.5-1.5B) from three families spanning under 3B to over 6B parameters.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the evidence-accumulation intuition and controlled setup, through the convergence theorem, to the answer-shift estimator and its empirical validation.
